title: The end of the year
steps: The voice has a name: Korvel. Long ago he wrote enchantments on the castle itself. At first he did it to make it better: safer, more comfortable, more magical. But little by little he slipped in changes so that the castle would obey him alone. Other wizards and I saw what he was doing, and we drove him out.

Your parents studied here. They were wizards, and among the best. They set about rewriting the castle's spells: they kept the good, so that it would go on teaching the new pupils every year and protecting wizards, and took out what Korvel had put in to control it.

Korvel came back to kill them. But your mother was already expecting you, and you, not yet born, protected them both. Korvel could kill only the magic in them. That is why they are not wizards now, and why they remember nothing.

The spells they had written were not yet finished, nor tied off. When your parents' magic died they came undone, and the castle's magic fell with them. And Korvel died with it: greedy for power, and seeking to live for ever, he had put all his magic, his own soul, into those spells. It took us whole years to mend Arvelia's magic. And we always believed Korvel was dead.
Today I am not sure. Perhaps his soul is held in the walls, in remnants of old spells that never quite vanished, waiting to take revenge and to rule the castle again. I do not know. But it may be.
Nobody says anything. At last, {mate}: "Then you beat him once already." And Orla: "And without knowing a single word yet."
Now the school knows, and nobody will listen to that voice alone again. Rinlo will help the teachers: he knows where it speaks.
The end-of-year dinner. Zarek sits beside Rinlo, grumbling: "If it scares you, I'll teach you. Slowly." Orla names you a pupil of Arvelia in your own right. The second year awaits.

"You began by taking a step. You end by describing creatures." Over the year you learned to give orders with their arguments, to cast spells and carry things, to keep values with a name and read what things know of themselves, to count cells, to wait and to choose with `if` and `else`, to repeat with `for` and `while`, to use lists, to fly, to write functions of your own with `def`, and at last classes, objects, `__init__`, inheriting and methods. {familiar} sleeps in your hood. The end of the first year.
